verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Firozabad's working-capital-light, fast-turnover imitation jewellery traders and job-work units with clean GST and tight stock control; avoid bridal-set inventory financiers and any borrower whose sales depend on one festival season.
title: Firozabad imitation jewellery: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Firozabad's Katra market sells gold-look rings and full bridal sets at retail price points from ₹25 up to ₹3,000, with rings at ₹100-500 [1][3]. **This is a copy-the-design, low-ticket, high-velocity trade, not a bullion business** — the shopkeeper's edge is design freshness and finish that does not fade, not metal value [1][3]. Cash comes in daily at the counter; value sits in finished stock and in the design pipeline, not in the raw material. So when a proposal lands, check the stock-to-sales ratio and the age of the oldest design lot; if stock is older than one season, ask what discount is being carried to clear it. ## Where the cash actually sits
Demand is explicitly seasonal — Diwali and the wedding season drive the pull, and gold and silver getting dearer pushes buyers toward the imitation alternative [1][2]. **A trader's year is a few strong weeks and many flat ones, so peak stock must be bought before the cash arrives.** That is the working-capital cycle to underwrite: short, repeatable, and self-liquidating within a season. Capex is light — this is trading and assembly, not a plant. Collect from customer the actual inventory days and the share of sales in the peak season; do not assume them. ## What has changed now
Local reporting is the only city-level evidence we have, and it is recent (October 2026) [1][2]. **The pull is real but it is a price-substitution story, not a volume boom** — buyers come because gold is unaffordable, and they will leave the same way. Rating commentary on jewellery flags intense competition from unorganised players limiting pricing flexibility and seasonality in demand [8]. The data pack shows India-wide bank credit +33.0% YoY against output +3.8% [D] — **system credit is running far ahead of real output, so our guardrail is structure, not optimism.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
Pursue the ring and daily-wear trader turning stock weekly, the job-work unit doing finishing for several shops, and the exporter with repeat Australia/Pakistan enquiries [3]. Take monthly GST returns, stock statements and counter-sales summaries; covenant a peak-season inventory cap and a minimum stock-turn. If a proposal shows receivables beyond 45 days, ask who the buyer is and why a counter-cash business is lending. ## Early warning signs
- Monthly GST turnover falling two months running (monthly) -> freeze fresh limits and inspect stock. - Stock statement showing design lots older than one season (monthly) -> demand a clearance plan before renewal. - Gold price softening and imitation demand thinning (quarterly) -> reprice the season's limit. - Cheque returns or delayed statutory dues (weekly) -> stop disbursement and review.
